content: Guaifenesin is a medication used to help loosen and thin mucus in the airways, making it easier to cough up and clear bronchial secretions. It is commonly used to make coughs more productive. General Disclaimer: WikiDoc is not a licensed healthcare provider and should not be used as a substitute for professional medical advice or care. It is intended solely as an educational resource. The content on WikiDoc drug pages is based on FDA package inserts, the National Library of Medicine, and clinical guidelines or consensus statements. WikiDoc does not endorse the use of any medication or device in a manner inconsistent with its labeling. Over-the-counter (OTC) medications are not always reviewed or approved by the FDA but may be marketed if they comply with applicable regulations. The FDA has not evaluated whether this product complies with such regulations. Common Adverse Reactions: Nausea and vomiting are the most frequently reported side effects. Adult Indications and Dosage: FDA-Labeled Indications: Guaifenesin is indicated to loosen phlegm (mucus) and thin bronchial secretions, facilitating a more productive cough. Dosage: Follow the recommended dosage or use as directed by a physician. Do not exceed six doses within a 24-hour period. Off-Label Use: There is limited information available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported uses of guaifenesin in adults. Pediatric Indications and Dosage: FDA-Labeled Indications: Guaifenesin is indicated to loosen phlegm (mucus) and thin bronchial secretions, making coughs more productive in pediatric patients. Dosage: Follow the recommended dosage or use as directed by a physician. Do not exceed six doses within a 24-hour period. Off-Label Use: There is limited information available regarding off-label guideline-supported or non-guideline-supported uses of guaifenesin in pediatric patients. Contraindications: There is limited information regarding specific contraindications for guaifenesin in the drug label. Warnings: Consult a doctor before use if you have: A cough that produces excessive mucus. A persistent or chronic cough, such as one associated with smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, or emphysema. Discontinue use and seek medical advice if: The cough lasts more than seven days, recurs, or is accompanied by fever, rash, or persistent headache, as these may indicate a more serious condition. Do not use if you are hypersensitive to any of the ingredients. If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Postmarketing Experience: Common gastrointestinal side effects include nausea and vomiting. Drug Interactions: Limited information is available regarding drug interactions with guaifenesin. Administration and Monitoring: Administration: Guaifenesin is administered orally. Monitoring: Limited information is available regarding monitoring requirements for guaifenesin. IV Compatibility: Limited information is available regarding the intravenous compatibility of guaifenesin. Overdosage: Limited information is available regarding guaifenesin overdose. If overdose or poisoning is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Alcohol Interaction: The interaction between alcohol and guaifenesin has not been established. Consult your doctor regarding the effects of consuming alcohol while taking this medication.
